Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http:/twww.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 81 s. 2023 28 December 2023 JENNIFER ANACIO Former Sangguniang Panlungsod Member Brgy. H - Tarusan, City of Borongan jennyanacio@gmail.com Dear Ms. Anacio: This has reference to your letter dated February 28, 2023 requesting for the Department's guidance regarding your salary and other emoluments attached to it (rice allowance, ACA/PERA, bonuses) during your time as Sangguniang Panlungsod Member for the period covering February 2019 to June 2019 which was allegedly withheld by the City Human Resource Officer without due process and order from an appropriate authority. Based on Opinion No. VIII-2020-01 issued by the Regional Office No. VIII of DILG Tacloban City dated January 15, 2020, that level ruled both in the negative as to matters raised before it, to wit: (1) whether SP Member Jennifer S. Anacio is still entitled to claim her salary considering that she has an authority to travel abroad issued by the DILG even without filing or having an approved leave of absence; and (2) whether there is a legal basis on her participation in the Sangguniang Panglungsod session through teleconference and that whether such participation in the session through teleconference shall be considered as part of her actual service even if she is outside the country. Consequently, in a letter dated January 18, 2021, you are now seeking reconsideration on the aforementioned legal opinion and requesting that the Department be apprised of the complete facts. Per your representations, you maintain the following: (1) The study abroad was with the knowledge and support of the City Mayor and the Sangguniang Panglungsod. The OIC, Office of the Human Resource Management Officer was likewise aware and has issued documents in support of your scholarship requirements. (2) You obtained the necessary Foreign Travel Authority (FTA) from the former DILG Secretary. This was endorsed by the Presiding Officer/Acting Vice-Mayor of Borongan with the required documents compliant with Item 5.5 of DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2018-197. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

(3) A Resolution was passed by the Sanggunian concerned which amended the Sanggunian Intemal Rules of Procedure and allowed participation and/or attendance of any member through teleconference. (4) On January 14, 2019, you were informed to have been excluded from the payroll of elected officials by the OIC-CHRMO without due notice or order. No formal communication or notice regarding the exclusion was provided. (5) The OIC, OCHRMO was allegedly in search for a legal basis of the teleconferencing or any document that would explicitly provide for the salary and benefits to which you are entitled to receive. You maintain that the nature of the work of an elected official is different and not based solely on attendance during sessions. The Local Govemment Code nor any regulation has fixed the office hours of elective officials for they as public officers are on call any time of the day. The OIC, OCHRMO advised you to just wait for the legal opinion of the regional office on the matter. (6) You maintain that it was the OIC, OCHRMO's burden to prove with sufficient evidence that she is not entitled to salary and other emoluments attached to it. Absent of such proof, the exclusion of payroll was premature and a violation of her right. (7) Further, the OIC, OCHRMO refused to accept your Application for leave contending that the matter has already been submitted to the DILG's regional office for its resolution. You submitted it to the Office of the Vice Mayor, since your application was not accepted by the OIC, OCHRMO. (8) You maintain that the the Property Clearance Accountability for Separation from the Service is not a condition sine qua non for the validity of the FTA, but a subsequent requirement to be complied with at the end of her term. Considering that her office was still operating at that time, it would be impractical and futile to comply with the same. Hence, this request. Notwithstanding the matters you have newly raised in your letter, we partly affirm the findings of the regional office. For purposes of reiteration, we provide that in addition to the discourse pertaining to DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2018-197 dated November 9, 2018, we cite Sec. 7.0 of the aforementioned circular, which provides the grounds for non-processing or disapproval of the request: 7.0 Grounds for Non-Processing or Disapproval of Request I. Incomplete administrative requirements shall not be processed and shall be returned to the concemed party without favorable action; 2. Any request submitted not within ten (IO) working days prior to the date of departure shall be automatically denied for processing. 4. No post-travel authority shall be issued. While you maintain that the travel abroad was with the knowledge and support of the City Mayor and the Sangguniang Panglungsod, it appears that there is no sufficient document to support this claim. Ultimately, the best document to prove this is through the approved leave of absence which was not secured prior to your travel. As Page 2 of 4

previously provided, the grant of an authority to travel abroad does not necessarily mean that there was already a prior or simultaneous or subsequent approval of a valid leave of absence. In addition, the travel authority issued by the DILG Secretary for the Australia trip contained a provision that needed to be complied with regarding the Property Clearance Accountability for Separation from the Service. In addition, the Certification from Property Accountability in lieu of the above mentioned document did not replace or satisfy the grant of travel authority by the DILG Secretary. However, as to your query on whether you are still entitled to claim your salaries and emoluments, we advise you to seek clarification from the Civil Service Commission as this matter is within their administrative competence. With regard to your participation in the Sanggunian sessions through teleconferencing, the Department had the occasion to opine the following in its DILG Opinion No. 50, s. of 2020 where it inferred on the requirement of physical presence to the sanggunian members when conducting a session, to wit: There is no law, rules and regulations, even RA 11469 or the Bayanihan to Heal as One Act which was passed primarily to address the COVID-19 pandemic and the Presidential Decrees issued by the Office of the President, which authorized the local sanggunians to conduct sessions through teleconferencing, video conferencing and other electronic means. Due to the absence of any law, rules and regulations, the following provisions of the LGC still govem the conduct of sanggunian members, to wit: SECTION 52. Sessions. - following the election (a) On the first day of the session immediately of its members, the Sanggunian shall, by resolution, fix the day, time, and place of its regular sessions. The minimum number of regular sessions shall be once a week for the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, Sangguniang Panlungsod, and Sangguniang bayan, and twice a Sangguniang Barangay. month for the (b) When public interest so demands, special sessions may be called by the local chief executive or by a majority of the members of the Sanggunian. (c) All Sanggunian sessions shall be open to the public unless a closed- door session is ordered by an affirmative vote of a majority of the members present, there being a quorum, in the public interest or for reasons of security, decency, or morality. No two (2) sessions, regular or special, may be held in a single day. (d) In the case of special sessions of the Sanggunian, a written notice to the members shall be served personally at the member's usual place of residence at least twenty- four (24) hours before the special session is held. Unless otherwise concurred in by two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Sanggunian members present, there beinq a quorum, no other matters may be considered at a special session except those stated in the notice. (e) Each Sanggunian shall keep a journal and record of its proceedings which may be published upon resolution of the Sanggunian concemed. SECTION 53. Quorum, - (a) A majority of all the members of the Sanggunian who have been elected and qualified shall constitute a quorum to transact 30 official business. Should a question of quorum be Page 3 of 4

raised during a session, the presiding officer shall immediately proceed to call the roll of the members and thereafter announce the results. (b) Where there is no quorum, the presiding officer may declare a recess until such time as a quorum is constituted, or a majority of the members present may adjourn from day to day and tten an f n e ber bsen witho stifiabl cause b esi natin membe of the San u ian s ed b member or members of the p_plice force assigned in the territorial urisdiction of the local ovemment unit concemed t arres pbsent member and Dresent him at the ses'ion. (c) If there is still no quorum despite the enforcement of the immediately preceding subsection, no business shall be transacted. The presiding officer, upon proper motion duly approved by the members present, shall then declare the session adjourned for lack of quorum. While there is also no categorical statement in the aforequoted provision of the Code requiring the physical presence of the sanggunian members to conduct a session, such physical presence can be inferred therefrom. [emphasis supplied) This opinion is being rendered based on the facts as represented and without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you on this matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. JUAN VICTOR R.
